title: Completion equivalence from bijective ideal-power quotient maps
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, f:A→B a ring homomorphism, and I⊆A and J⊆B ideals with I⊆f⁻¹(J). Suppose the canonical maps A/I^n→B/J^n induced by f are bijective for every natural n. Then there is a ring equivalence E between their respective adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] such that for every n and x, the n-th coordinate of E(x) is the canonical quotient map applied to the n-th coordinate of x. No locality, Noetherian or nonzero-ring hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Replace the canonical bijective quotient maps by ring equivalences e_n. They commute with quotient reductions, checked on representatives. Applying e_m to the corresponding desired equation proves that the inverse equivalences also commute with reductions.

Lift the compatible families e_n∘eval_n and e_n⁻¹∘eval_n to ring maps F and G between the two completions. Quotient evaluation compatibility follows from the compatible-sequence construction (or by induction on a representative adic Cauchy sequence). Evaluating FG and GF at every n proves both are identities; the lift evaluation formula supplies the claimed coordinates. At n=0 the quotients are zero rings; no positivity or proper-ideal assumption was used.

lean.statement:
theorem equiv_of_powerQuotient_bijective
    {A : Type*} {B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (I : Ideal A) (J : Ideal B) (h : I ≤ J.comap f)
    (hbij : ∀ n : ℕ, Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap (J ^ n) f
        ((pow_le_pow_left' h n).trans (Ideal.le_comap_pow f n)))) :
    ∃ E : AdicCompletion I A ≃+* AdicCompletion J B,
      ∀ n x, AdicCompletion.evalₐ J n (E x) =
        Ideal.quotientMap (J ^ n) f
          ((pow_le_pow_left' h n).trans (Ideal.le_comap_pow f n))
          (AdicCompletion.evalₐ I n x)
